severity_notes:
- An acked `Durable` record that is not on disk, or does not replay after a crash, is severe. So is anything that lets two daemons own one `wab_dir`.
- A change to the on-disk WAB format, the wire protocol or a published crate's public API without a version decision is severe: it needs the owner (semver, the `docs_drift` guards).
- A panic reachable from a client frame, a stored segment or a config value is critical.
- A secret (sink URL credentials, bearer token, crates.io token) reaching a log, a `Debug` string, argv or `/status` is critical.
- Anything that loosens a security default (peer UID check, socket permissions, mTLS on TCP) is severe, and is never fixed overnight without the owner.

Scope of this epic (from its spec, docs/superpowers/temper/cleanup-2026-11/spec.md): the whole repository at the branch tip, NOT only `git diff main...epic/cleanup-2026-11` (the branch starts equal to main, so that diff is just the spec). Review the code itself, in your lens's area (the spec's Scope table). A finding needs an input and a wrong result that a verifier can reproduce; style, refactors and perf ideas are not findings.
These are owner items (kind owner), never fixes: a change to the WAB or `.confirmed` format, the wire protocol, `--json` shapes or a published crate's public API; loosening a security default; a new or upgraded dependency; D10 (explicit missing --config only WARNs: a deferred owner decision).
build_rule:
Every build, test, clippy or gate on beast runs as a jobq job: never run cargo, a gate script or a test binary directly in your ssh session (beast's ~/agents/CLAUDE.md; a session that compiled outside jobq was OOM-killed). Work in a worktree under ~/work/weir/ on beast; jobq's --cwd is that worktree's physical path (`pwd -P`).

Submit, then wait in the foreground (a single Bash call must stay under 10 minutes, so never use `jobq run` for a gate, and never end your turn while a job of yours is queued or running):
  ssh beast 'cd <worktree> && JOBQ_SUBMITTER=temper-cleanup ~/.local/bin/jobq submit --profile rust --project weir --cores 4 --mem 4G --timeout 3h --cwd "$(pwd -P)" --name <your-label>-quick -- bash .temper/gate-quick.sh'
  ssh beast '~/.local/bin/jobq wait <id>'   (call it again, with a Bash timeout of 600000 ms, until the job ends; its exit status is the gate's)
The full gate is the same with `--mem 8G --timeout 5h --name <your-label>-full -- bash .temper/gate-full.sh`. One cargo command (a reproduction, a single test) is the same with `--mem 4G --timeout 1h --name <your-label>-run -- bash .temper/gate-run.sh <cargo args>`, e.g. `... -- bash .temper/gate-run.sh test -p weir-wab segment`.
A job's env is cleared: pass variables as `-- env VAR=value bash .temper/gate-run.sh ...`. Read results from `~/.local/bin/jobq logs <id> --tail 400` (it prints only the last 200 lines by default) and from the gate's summary, /srv/bulk/Projects/weir/logs/gate/<worktree dir name>/latest-<quick|full|run>/summary.txt, whose last line is `GATE <name> rc=N`. A job's peak memory includes page cache: if a job is OOM-killed, resubmit once with a 2G larger --mem and say so in your result. Never cancel or touch another submitter's jobs. Keep at most one job of yours queued or running at a time. Beast's rule is at most 4 builds of this run at once: before each submit, run `ssh beast 'JOBQ_SUBMITTER=temper-cleanup ~/.local/bin/jobq list --mine | grep -cE " (queued|running) "'`; while it prints 4 or more, wait with `ssh beast 'sleep 120'` and check again.
Never set CARGO_TARGET_DIR or make another target dir: the gate slots are the build dirs; a gate that waits for a slot or for jobq's memory is normal. Never run sudo, never run the chaos harness's power-cut campaign, never touch docker images, volumes or containers that aren't weir's, never write the CI-skip token in a commit message. Commits carry only the `Temper-Task` trailer: no Co-Authored-By, Claude-Session or "Generated with" lines. Never print a secret or token.
A fix also adds one line under CHANGELOG.md `## [Unreleased]` (replace its "Nothing yet." line), in `### Fixed`, or `### Changed` for a behaviour an operator can notice, in the file's existing style. The `docs_drift` and `demo_drift` tests guard figures and version strings in the docs: if a fix trips one, fix the doc, never weaken the guard.
Clean up what you start on beast (test processes, tmux servers); leave worktrees in place.

selected.summary: ClickHouse's insert_deduplication_token and the HTTP sink's NDJSON-batch Idempotency-Key are the batch's content-only DedupToken, so two distinct batches with byte-identical records share a key and the downstream silently drops the later one (sinks-r3-01, sinks-r3-02).
selected.input: sink_type=clickhouse with a MergeTree/Replicated*MergeTree dedup window, or sink_type=http with sink_http_batch="ndjson" and sink_send_idempotency_key=true against an endpoint that honours Idempotency-Key. A producer sends the same record at low rate (a heartbeat {"status":"ok"} every 30 s), so successive timed-seal segments drain as one-record batches with identical bytes.
selected.wrong_result: Every such batch carries the same key (sha256 over len+bytes, no WAB coordinate). ClickHouse treats the second as a duplicate block and inserts nothing with HTTP 200; the idempotent HTTP endpoint replays its cached 2xx. The sink returns Ok, the drain confirms and deletes the segment, and the acked records are lost with no error or dead letter. The S3 sink's key (segment created_at + first RecordId + count, crates/weir-sink-s3/src/key.rs batch_name) and HTTP per-record mode (RecordId since 2.0.2) already avoid this.

selected.summary: weir-server system::sigterm_unlinks_the_socket_at_once_and_metrics_stay_up_until_exit failed once in a quick gate (ECONNRESET instead of EOF on an idle connection at system.rs:6183; jq-01M6V6SJAE0K2G3Z0SZHZQQRJJ) and passed on a rerun and in three full gates and CI.
selected.input: Run that one test repeatedly under load on beast, e.g. 100 iterations through `bash .temper/gate-run.sh test -p weir-server --test system sigterm_unlinks_the_socket_at_once_and_metrics_stay_up_until_exit`, inside a loop in one jobq job (cores 4, mem 4G, timeout 1h).
selected.wrong_result: The test fails intermittently with ECONNRESET where it asserts EOF on an idle connection after SIGTERM: either the test asserts something the daemon doesn't promise (an idle connection may be reset rather than cleanly closed during shutdown), or the daemon resets a connection it should close cleanly.

selected.summary: The workflow_dispatch trigger is documented as 'deploy the site on demand', but both the Pages upload step and the deploy job only run when github.event_name == 'push'. A manual run builds the book and publishes nothing.
selected.input: Actions -> "Publish docs" -> "Run workflow" on main (event_name = workflow_dispatch), for example after enabling Pages or after a main push that touched no watched path, which are the cases the comment at lines 8-10 names.
selected.wrong_result: The build job runs, the upload-pages-artifact step is skipped (line 63: `if: github.event_name == 'push' && ...`) and the deploy job is skipped (line 78: same condition). The site is not deployed, which contradicts the trigger's documented purpose.

selected.summary: SETUP.md is written for every schedule saying 'Phase 1 — random kill -9 only ... dm-flakey injection is unimplemented ... says nothing about power loss'. run-soak.sh line 25 prints '(Phase 1: kill -9 only)' the same way. Both claims are false for power_loss and lifecycle-trigger schedules, which do cut power through dm-flakey.
selected.input: `./run-soak.sh schedules/shutdown-bounded.toml fnd-shutdown-bounded 25200`, the invocation the PR-9 plan documents. That schedule has dm_target = "flakey", kind = "sigterm_at" and cut = "power_loss", and faults.cut_mode returns "power_loss". The same happens with any powerloss-*.toml schedule.
selected.wrong_result: The run's own provenance records say it was a kill -9-only run with no dm-flakey and no power-loss coverage: runs/<id>/SETUP.md and the console.log banner. The episodes were actually power cuts judged under fault="power_loss", so anyone reading the archived run directory gets the wrong fault class.

selected.summary: mount_options() looks up the WAB filesystem in /proc/mounts by device name and takes the first match. On tmpfs, overlay or any bind-mounted device it reports another mount's options in the environment header that bare-metal claims cite.
selected.input: Run deploy/run_bare_metal_bench.sh on beast, where /tmp (the default TMPDIR) is tmpfs.
selected.wrong_result: `df /tmp` gives device 'tmpfs', and the first tmpfs line in /proc/mounts is /run. The header then prints 'Mount opts: rw,nosuid,nodev,size=6558452k,nr_inodes=819200,mode=755,inode64' (/run's options), not /tmp's 'rw,nosuid,nodev,nr_inodes=1048576,inode64,usrquota'. Shown on beast. The fix is to match on the mount point (`df --output=target` or `findmnt -no OPTIONS -T`).

selected.summary: The smoke test says it pushes and acks 30 records across three durability tiers. push_simple pushes only two tiers (Durable, Buffered), so the count is 20.
selected.wrong_result: It prints 'Pushing 10 records per durability tier (30 total)...' and 'All 30 records acked.' after 20 records were pushed, because the Batched tier was retired and crates/weir-client/examples/push_simple.rs lists two tiers. The header comment ('all three durability tiers') is also wrong.

selected.summary: The under_wab_dir check compares the admin socket path lexically against the canonicalized wab_dir, so an admin_socket_path reached through a symlinked spelling of wab_dir is accepted, and the socket is bound inside the WAB.
selected.input: wab_dir=/data/wab, where /data is a symlink to /mnt/x (canonical wab_dir /mnt/x/wab), with admin_socket_path=/data/wab/admin.sock.
selected.wrong_result: from_layers accepts the path (/data/wab/admin.sock does not start with /mnt/x/wab), and the admin socket is created inside wab_dir. The rule 'put the admin socket outside the WAB' should refuse it with under_wab_dir.

selected.summary: The 'not a valid sink type' error lists the valid types without s3, which is a supported sink.
selected.wrong_result: The error says "expected 'noop', 'http', 'mysql', 'postgres', or 'clickhouse'" and omits 's3', which --help and SinkType::parse both accept.

selected.summary: FEATURE_GATED_FLAGS lacks --sink-mysql-id-column and --sink-postgres-id-column, so on a build without the matching feature these flags get the generic 'unknown arguments' error, not the feature-naming message that --help NOTES promises.
selected.input: A build with --no-default-features --features http-sink, run as `weir-server --sink-mysql-id-column id`
selected.wrong_result: `unknown arguments: ["--sink-mysql-id-column", "id"]` instead of "flag '--sink-mysql-id-column' requires the 'mysql-sink' feature ...". --help states that passing a feature-gated flag is 'rejected with a message naming the feature to rebuild with'.

selected.summary: Every DST invariant failure prints a repro command, `WEIR_DST_SEED=<seed> cargo test -p weir-server --features dst dst::`, and docs/architecture.md:338 promises the same. Nothing in the tree reads WEIR_DST_SEED, so the printed repro never replays the failing seed.
selected.input: The CI `dst` job runs `WEIR_DST_SWEEP=300` (ci.yml:240-244) and the sweep's fixed SplitMix64 stream reaches a seed past index 16 that violates an invariant. The panic prints `reproduce: WEIR_DST_SEED=0x... cargo test -p weir-server --features dst dst::`. The developer runs exactly that line.
selected.wrong_result: WEIR_DST_SEED is ignored: `grep -rn WEIR_DST_SEED crates` finds only the panic format string (dst.rs:930) and the module doc (dst.rs:19), and the only env read in dst.rs is WEIR_DST_SWEEP (dst.rs:2500). The command reruns the default 16-seed sweep plus the pinned seeds and passes green while the durability violation is still there. The failing seed is never replayed or pinned. The panic also does not print the Fault/Scenario/records, so the seed alone could not rebuild a SimSpec even if the variable were read.

selected.summary: When the startup WAB scan fails, the placeholder reject flag goes through the cap hysteresis, so ingest stays refused below the cap after a scan succeeds
selected.input: wab_max_bytes = 1000. The startup scan in startup_cap_gate fails (compute_wab_bytes_on_disk returns None), so wab_cap_rejecting is set to true. The first 5 s poll scan then succeeds with bytes = 950 (below the cap, at or above low water 900). Unit form: startup_cap_gate(Path::new("/nonexistent"), 1000, &board, &metrics); then crate::wab::cap::evaluate(1000, 950, &board.wab_cap_rejecting).
selected.wrong_result: evaluate returns true and the flag stays set, because `was == true` applies `bytes >= low_water`. Pushes keep being nacked and /readyz stays 503 wab_cap_rejecting, although the daemon never saw the WAB at or over its cap. With the sink down, nothing drains below 900 and the refusal never ends. The function's doc ('start rejecting until a poll scan succeeds') and its WARN line ('pushes nack (fail-closed) until a scan succeeds') both promise a release on the first successful scan.

selected.summary: When the daemon refuses a whole PushBatch at admission (WAB cap or ownership lost), the nack counters go up by 1 per frame, not by the record count. The batch success path counts per record, and the code comment at line 492 says these are per-record counters.
selected.input: wab_max_bytes exceeded (cap rejecting). Producer sends one PushBatch of 100 records.
selected.wrong_result: weir_records_nack_total{reason=internal_error} and weir_records_nack_internal_total{cause=wab_cap} each go up by 1 instead of 100, so rate panels undercount rejected records by up to the batch size.

selected.summary: The TS demo client handles Ack and HealthCheckResponse in one branch. A push answered with a HealthCheckResponse resolves as {acked:true}, and a healthCheck answered with an Ack also resolves. The Rust reference client treats both as a desync and poisons.
selected.input: A peer (desynced or non-conformant) answers a Push frame with a HealthCheckResponse (0x05).
selected.wrong_result: client.push() resolves {acked:true} for a record that was never acked (false ack). Expected: reject as a desync and fail the connection.

selected.summary: The TS demo (and the Python demo at demos/py-wire-client/src/weir_wire/client.py:164) maps a Nack with an empty payload to InternalError, the one transient, keep-open reason. The Rust reference client treats it as a protocol desync and poisons.
selected.input: A peer sends a Nack frame with payload_len 0.
selected.wrong_result: The TS client rejects with NackError(InternalError) and closesConnection = false, so callers keep using a desynced stream. The Python client raises a retryable NackError(INTERNAL_ERROR). Expected: a desync error that closes the connection.

answers.dedup-coordinate-key: Owner, 8 Nov: fix this in PR #77; this is an approved contract change. Contract: (1) one shared helper in crates/weir-server/src/sink/ derives a batch key from the SinkBatch's segment context, exactly the S3 sink's coordinate: segment_created_at (unix ns) + the first record's RecordId + the record count, hashed with sha256 to a fixed-length hex (document the exact preimage format in the helper's doc and in docs/sinks/ for both sinks). It must be stable across replays of the same batch (same segment, same batch boundaries), and differ for distinct segments even when the bytes match. (2) When the batch has no record_ids or no segment_created_at (a SinkBatch built with SinkBatch::new, e.g. a sink author's test), fall back to the existing DedupToken, so that path is unchanged. (3) ClickHouse sends the new key as insert_deduplication_token; the HTTP sink's NDJSON batch mode sends `Idempotency-Key: sha256:<key>`. HTTP per-record mode is unchanged (RecordId). (4) Replace clickhouse.rs's `dedup_token_is_unchanged_from_weir_1_x` with a test that pins the new derivation, and add tests that two byte-identical batches from different segments get different keys while a replay of the same batch gets the same key. Leave weir-sink-sdk's DedupToken and its own 1.x pin test untouched: no public API change in weir-sink-sdk. (5) CHANGELOG `### Changed`: both keys changed; after upgrading, a batch that was in flight at the upgrade is re-sent once under the new key, so ClickHouse and an idempotent HTTP endpoint may see it twice, once. Update docs/operations/configuration.md and the sink docs where they describe the token/Idempotency-Key.
answers.sigterm-system-flake: Owner, 8 Nov: investigate this possible flake. First reproduce it: loop the single test (at least 100 runs) in one jobq job, and read the test and the shutdown path to decide which side is wrong. If it reproduces: if the daemon's documented contract allows a reset on an idle connection at shutdown, fix the test to accept both EOF and ECONNRESET there (and say why in a comment); if the daemon should close cleanly, fix the daemon with a failing test first. Never add a retry loop or a sleep. If it does not reproduce in 100+ runs, change nothing and return status blocked with reason 'not reproduced: <runs, job id>'.
